bug_semantics: picklescan disassembles pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL references and uses a denylist to decide which imports count as dangerous findings. Before 0.0.35, _io.FileIO and urllib.request.urlopen were absent from that denylist, so their imports produced no dangerous issue/infected-file result. A pickle that downstream code trusts and unpickles can invoke _io.FileIO to open an arbitrary local file, then pass that file object as the iterable POST body to urllib.request.urlopen, combining arbitrary file read with attacker-chosen outbound SSRF/exfiltration while bypassing the scanner's RCE-focused entries such as builtins.open, os, and exec.
flaw_origin: c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e is the smallest real BIC: it first adds src/picklescan/scanner.py and implements the vulnerable denylist rule in scan_pickle_bytes, incrementing issues_count only when a parsed global matches _suspicious_globals; the new map omits both _io.FileIO and urllib.request.urlopen. Later refactors renamed/expanded the map but preserved that fail-open-for-unlisted-dangerous-globals behavior. Its direct parent 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326 has no scanner.py, so this is not a move, refactor, revert, release commit, or squash aggregate.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file -p c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e` shows author and committer `Matthieu Maitre <mmaitre314@users.noreply.github.com>` and the complete message `Implement Pickle scanner`; the commit object has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI trailer/marker, and neither identity is a bot.
evidence: First-party GHSA-9726-w42j-3qjr states affected `<v0.0.35`, patched `v0.0.35`, and gives the io.FileIO -> urllib.request.urlopen file-read/exfiltration PoC. In the clone, `git show 323bd004691e442b109b00a1251cd9acc1a4be98:src/picklescan/scanner.py` shows the v0.0.34 parent classifies a raw global as Dangerous and increments issues_count only when it matches _unsafe_globals; otherwise an unlisted global is merely Suspicious, and ScanResult.infected_files is `1 if issues_count > 0 else 0`. `git grep -n -E '(_io|urllib\.request|FileIO|urlopen)' 323bd004691e442b109b00a1251cd9acc1a4be98 -- src/picklescan tests` returns no matches. `git diff 323bd004691e442b109b00a1251cd9acc1a4be98 a01c58d5dd7960db557b849817c0ab83ab111ef1 -- src/picklescan/scanner.py setup.cfg` adds `_io: {FileIO}` and `urllib.request: *` to _unsafe_globals and changes 0.0.34 to 0.0.35; `git log -S` for each exact new entry identifies only a01c58d5dd7960db557b849817c0ab83ab111ef1. `git rev-parse v0.0.34^{commit} v0.0.35^{commit}` returns 323bd004691e442b109b00a1251cd9acc1a4be98 then a01c58d5dd7960db557b849817c0ab83ab111ef1, and ancestry checks succeed. For origin, `git log --all --reverse -S 'filter = _suspicious_globals.get(g[0])' -- src/picklescan/scanner.py` and `git log -L 69,85:src/picklescan/scanner.py c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e` identify c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e as the first writer of the match-only issue rule; its setup.cfg says version 0.0.1. `git diff-tree --name-status 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326 c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e -- src/picklescan/scanner.py` reports `A`, and `git ls-tree -r 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326 src/picklescan` has no scanner, directly proving parent absence. `git cat-file -p` supplies the BIC parent, human identities, complete message, and marker absence.
reasoning: The vulnerable behavior begins with the first functional scanner, not with a later denylist expansion or the 0.0.35 release/fix commit: c1d5abd introduces both the security promise and the match-only denylist implementation that lets these executable globals pass without a dangerous finding, while the parent tree has no scanner implementation. The advisory fix directly closes both required legs of the published chain in one commit/tag. Because the BIC is an ordinary single-parent human-authored commit whose commit object contains no AI attribution or bot identity, the BIC-only policy requires NOT_AI; any evidence associated with the later fix or PR is irrelevant.
